items.item: Every status column heading shows the status name and its ticket count, and the count equals the cards shown or the column states how many are not shown (such as "Showing 20 of 134")
items.evidence:
Column header template: `

${status.label}

${visible.length}${visible.length !== all.length ? ' / ' + all.length : ''}` — shows e.g. "New 5" when unfiltered, and "3 / 5" style fraction when filters hide cards.

items.item: Each card shows the ticket number (such as #4821), subject, customer, priority as a word or code (such as "P1 · Urgent") and the assignee, or an explicit "Unassigned"
items.evidence: cardHtml() renders `${ticket.id}` (e.g. TCK-4825), `${ticket.subject}`, `${ticket.company} · ${ticket.contact}`, `${pm.label}` (e.g. "Urgent"), and assigneeHtml which prints the assignee name or the italic text "Unassigned" when `ticket.assignee` is null.

items.item: Open tickets show the time left to the next SLA target and which target it is (such as "Resolution due in 2h 15m"), and breached tickets show how long they are overdue (such as "Breached 40m ago") in text or with an icon, not by colour alone
items.evidence: slaInfo() only ever produces generic text: `${formatDuration(diff)} left` (e.g. "55m left") or `Overdue ${formatDuration(diff)}` (e.g. "Overdue 1h 40m"). There is only one undifferentiated dueAt per ticket and the text never names which SLA target (first response vs. resolution) is being counted.

items.item: Tickets in a waiting status (such as "Waiting on customer") show their SLA timer as paused instead of counting down
items.evidence: slaInfo(ticket) branches only on `ticket.status === 'resolved'` vs. everything else; waiting-status tickets (e.g. TCK-4795, TCK-4788) are run through the same `diff = ticket.dueAt - now` countdown/breach logic as 'new' and 'progress' tickets — no paused state exists in code or in the screenshot (TCK-4795 shows "Overdue 1h 40m", TCK-4788 shows "4h 0m left").

items.item: Within each column the cards are ordered by SLA due time or by priority, and the board states which ordering is used
items.evidence: render() does `tickets.filter(t => t.status === status.key).filter(matchesFilters)` with no `.sort()` call — cards stay in raw array insertion order. In the 'New' column this yields dueAt 55m, 45m, 20m, 6h, 26h (not sorted ascending or descending by due time, only loosely grouped by priority). No ordering label appears anywhere in the header markup.

items.item: Search finds tickets by number, subject or customer, and filters cover assignee (including "Me" and "Unassigned"), priority and SLA state (such as breached or due within 1 hour)
items.evidence: matchesFilters() builds `hay` from `${ticket.subject} ${ticket.company} ${ticket.contact}` only — ticket.id is never included, so searching "4821" finds nothing. agentFilter options are populated from AGENT_COLORS plus an 'Unassigned' option, but there is no 'Me' option. There is no SLA-state filter control at all (no breached / due-within-1h option).

items.item: Each card has keyboard-reachable actions to assign the ticket (including "Assign to me") and to change its status without dragging, with accessible names that include the ticket number
items.evidence: A focusable `<select id="move-${ticket.id}" data-move-select>` with label "Move ${ticket.id} to a different status" covers the status-change requirement, but no assign control (no button/select for assignee, no "Assign to me") exists anywhere in cardHtml().

items.item: An empty column shows a short message instead of blank space, a search or filter with no matches offers to clear it, and loading and failed-load (with retry) states exist
items.evidence:
Empty/filtered columns render `

No matching tickets

`, satisfying the empty-message part, but there is no 'clear filters' affordance anywhere. boardMeta briefly says "Loading tickets…" (line 67) but render() runs synchronously with no async fetch, so no real loading state, and no failed-load/retry UI exists in the markup or script.

items.item: Every relative time (such as "Updated 3h ago") also exposes the exact date, time and timezone, in a <time datetime> element or a title attribute
items.evidence: SLA and resolved-time strings (e.g. "${formatDuration(diff)} left", "Resolved ${formatDuration(ago)} ago") are rendered as plain `<span>` text with no `<time datetime>` element and no `title` attribute carrying an absolute timestamp anywhere in cardHtml().

notes: This board is unusually template-tell-free: no gradients, no glass/blur, no emoji, no uppercase tracked labels, no sidebar, no decorative charts, small/consistent border radius (2-4px per audit), and no hover-lift effects were found in the markup or CSS. The automated audit's main flags are text-contrast failures (40 instances, e.g. p#boardMeta at 4.05:1 and several card sub-text spans at 2.4-3.2:1) and one font-size-base warning (15px h3 body text vs. 13-14px expected), plus a type-scale warning for 8 distinct font sizes — these are visual-polish issues, not checklist items, but worth flagging since contrast failures also touch the SLA badges relied on for the (failing) SLA-target-identification checklist item.
